newsitem.title: UK: British Steel profits slump, pound a concern.
newsitem.headline: British Steel profits slump, pound a concern.

text.p: British Steel Plc voiced concern about the long term impact of the strong pound on future profits on Monday after seeing last year's profitability decimated by the rise in sterling.

After reporting year pretax profits halving to 451 million pounds ($737 million) from 1.1 billion the previous year, Sir Brian Moffat, chairman, said: "The steel trading outlook for 1997/98 is one of cautious optimism, although concerns remain about the current strength of sterling and its serious impact on our future profits."
British Steel unveiled new cost cutting initiatives including a job cutting programme.

The profit slump had been widely expected and was in line with analysts' forecasts. The total dividend payout stood frozen at 10 pence per share and sales were up two percent at 7.22 billion pounds ($11.8 billion).

British Steel's latest cost cutting drive will comprise of further cutbacks in staff, although the company failed to quantify how many jobs would go. Though in recent press reports British Steel has suggested that it could be as high as 10,000 jobs over five years. In recent years the group has reduced its headcount by between 500 and 1,000 a year.
It also plans to drive down the cost of raw materials, supplies and services and make better use of information technology.

In the results statement, Moffat described the past year as "a difficult one" due to the double whammy of currency levels and weak steel prices in its major markets. But he said current trading was enjoying "buoyant" demand in Britain, the U.S. and the Far East. Mainland Europe, which has inflicted the greatest pain on British Steel's profitability, was also seeing some improvement, he said. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
